work_items.title: Pure nearest-eligible-driver selector (Common/Dispatch) with unit tests
acceptance_criteria: A new PURE static helper Common/Dispatch/NearestDriverSelector.SelectNearest(...) takes: an IReadOnlyCollection<DriverCandidate> candidates, pickupLat/pickupLng (double), maxRadiusKm (int), now (DateTimeOffset), staleThreshold (TimeSpan), and an exclusion set (IReadOnlySet<Guid> excludedDriverIds). It returns the single nearest ELIGIBLE, non-excluded candidate (as DriverCandidate? or a small result), or null when none qualify. NO I/O, no DbContext, no DI — same purity discipline as OrderStateMachine / HaversineDistance.

DriverCandidate is a public record carrying exactly the fields the predicate needs: DriverId (Guid), CurrentVehicleId (Guid?), Status (DriverStatus), LastLat (double?), LastLng (double?), LastPositionAt (DateTimeOffset?). No entity leaks in — the job projects Driver rows into DriverCandidate.

Eligibility predicate (ALL must hold): Status == DriverStatus.Free (Free ONLY — Offline/EnRoute/Busy are ineligible; EnRoute/Busy are active-ride states, Offline is off-shift); LastLat, LastLng and LastPositionAt are all non-null; LastPositionAt >= now - staleThreshold (fresh position; the freshness check is NOT redundant with StalePositionJob because AutoDispatch ticks at 5 s and StalePositionJob at 60 s, so a driver may be Free-but-stale for up to ~1 min); the driver id is NOT in excludedDriverIds; haversine distance (via Common/Geo/HaversineDistance.Meters) from pickup to (LastLat, LastLng) <= maxRadiusKm * 1000.

Among all candidates passing the predicate, the one with the SMALLEST haversine distance is returned. Ties (identical distance) resolve deterministically (e.g. by DriverId) — document the tiebreak in an XML remark. When the candidate collection is empty or none pass, return null.

staleThreshold is a PARAMETER (caller passes TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5) to mirror StalePositionJob.StaleThreshold) — do NOT hardcode 5 min inside the selector, and do NOT reference StalePositionJob from Common/. maxRadiusKm is an int (matches FleetSettings.MaxOfferRadiusKm).
test_cases: SelectNearest_SingleEligibleInRadius_ReturnsThatDriver: one Free, fresh, in-radius candidate → returned.
SelectNearest_TwoEligible_ReturnsCloser: two Free fresh in-radius candidates at different distances → the nearer one is returned (nearest-first, spec test case 2).
SelectNearest_DriverOutsideRadius_Excluded: a Free fresh candidate just beyond maxRadiusKm*1000 m → not returned; when it is the only candidate, returns null (spec test case 3).
SelectNearest_OfflineDriver_Excluded and SelectNearest_EnRouteOrBusyDriver_Excluded: non-Free statuses never returned (spec test case 6).
SelectNearest_StalePosition_Excluded: LastPositionAt older than now - staleThreshold → not returned (spec test case 6).
SelectNearest_NullPosition_Excluded: LastLat/LastLng/LastPositionAt null → not returned.
SelectNearest_ExcludedDriver_Skipped: the nearest candidate is in excludedDriverIds → the NEXT-nearest eligible is returned instead (spec test case 4 unit-level).
SelectNearest_NoEligible_ReturnsNull: empty collection and all-ineligible collection both return null.
SelectNearest_EqualDistance_DeterministicTiebreak: two equidistant eligible candidates → the same one is chosen every call.
work_items.notes: Pure unit tests only — NO Testcontainers, NO TaxiApiFactory, NO Docker. Placement in Common/Dispatch/ is a conscious single-consumer exception justified like OrderStateMachine (a pure domain class in Common/Orders/): a pure, testable decision module the job composes. This WI exists FIRST so its unit tests precede the job's integration tests (rules/web-testing test-ordering ladder equivalent: pure logic before integration). The selector owns the COMPLETE eligibility predicate so spec eligibility cases (2,3,6) are proven at the fast unit level; WI-2 only wires DB projection + tenant scope + OrderService around it.

work_items.title: AutoDispatchJob — scan New orders, offer nearest eligible driver via OrderService, DI wiring, integration tests
acceptance_criteria: New internal sealed AutoDispatchJob : BackgroundService with the SAME ctor shape as OfferTimeoutJob (IServiceScopeFactory scopeFactory, TimeProvider timeProvider, ILogger<AutoDispatchJob> logger). ExecuteAsync is a thin PeriodicTimer(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5), timeProvider) → await RunTickAsync shell with the SAME try/catch (LogError on unhandled tick, rethrow OperationCanceledException by exclusion). All per-tick logic lives in a public Task RunTickAsync(CancellationToken ct) called directly by integration tests.

SCAN phase (one scope, IgnoreQueryFilters, AsNoTracking, cross-tenant system scan): select candidate orders with Status == OrderStatus.New that are (a) old enough — CreatedAt + AutoDispatchAfterSeconds <= now — AND (b) NOT future-scheduled: (o.ScheduledAt == null || o.ScheduledAt <= now). [CONFIRMED FINDING: CreateOrderEndpoint persists a future-ScheduledAt order as Status=New immediately with NO hold mechanism, so without this guard a ride scheduled for tomorrow would be auto-assigned 60 s after creation.] Read per-fleet AutoDispatchEnabled, AutoDispatchAfterSeconds, MaxOfferRadiusKm from FleetSettings using the (int?)-cast projection guard EXACTLY like OfferTimeoutJob (a NULLABLE projected value distinguishes a missing settings row from a real 0). Project minimal columns: (OrderId, FleetId, PickupLat, PickupLng) plus the per-fleet settings. Compute the CreatedAt + AutoDispatchAfterSeconds <= now comparison in memory (mirror OfferTimeoutJob avoiding EF DateTimeOffset-arithmetic translation issues).

GATING (asymmetric vs OfferTimeoutJob): a missing FleetSettings row → SKIP the order (treated as auto-dispatch disabled), NOT a default. Project AutoDispatchEnabled as (bool?) — a null projection (no row) and false both fail the '== true' check, so 'AutoDispatchEnabled != true → SKIP' covers explicitly-disabled AND missing-row in one comparison. AutoDispatchAfterSeconds and MaxOfferRadiusKm are read via the (int?) cast so a null projection means 'no row → skip', never 0. Prefer a SINGLE nullable-settings projection (one row read into a nullable-tuple / anonymous shape) over three correlated subqueries — the three fields live in the same FleetSettings row. Note: unlike OfferTimeoutJob which defaults a missing timeout to 45 s, AutoDispatch has NO safe default because gating is opt-in.

PER-ORDER phase (one FRESH scope per order — a poisoned change-tracker from a StaleVersion/IllegalTransition must not leak to the next order): resolve the concrete CurrentTenant, set tenant.FleetId = order.FleetId (mirror OfferTimeoutJob.TimeoutOrderAsync EXACTLY), resolve TaxiDbContext and OrderService from that scope. Inside this tenant scope, query Drivers (AsNoTracking — the query filter gives fleet isolation for free) and project into DriverCandidate for NearestDriverSelector.

EXCLUSION SET derived from order_events for THIS order: [CONFIRMED FROM OrderStateMachine] Assigned events carry a NULL payload (no driver id) — do NOT read a driver id off Assigned rows. Only Declined ({declinedDriverId, reason}) and Timeout ({timedOutDriverId, reason}) event payloads carry the driver id. Load the Declined + Timeout OrderEvents for the order with ToListAsync FIRST, then parse the JsonDocument payloads IN MEMORY (per the CLAUDE.md rule: you cannot project Payload.RootElement inside a LINQ Select — it does not translate and 500s). Collect declinedDriverId / timedOutDriverId into a HashSet<Guid>. This exclusion set is COMPLETE because the only Assigned→New paths are Decline and Timeout, both of which write the id.

DRIVER SELECTION: call NearestDriverSelector.SelectNearest(candidates, order.PickupLat, order.PickupLng, maxRadiusKm, now, TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5), exclusionSet). staleThreshold = 5 min mirrors StalePositionJob. If null (no eligible driver), leave the order New and LogDebug a no-driver skip with a Reason (e.g. "NoEligibleDriver") — never spam, never error. Consider excluding drivers who are already the DriverId of another order currently in Assigned status for the fleet (pending-offer window — see Assumptions); implement per the chosen assumption.

OFFER via OrderService ONLY (never set order.Status; never publish from the job): build new AssignPayload(candidate.DriverId, candidate.CurrentVehicleId) (mirror AssignOrderEndpoint) and call orderService.TransitionAsync(orderId, OrderTransition.Assign, Actor.System, payload, ct). On success LogInformation with OrderId, DriverId, FleetId (event-style, present tense, no PII beyond ids). OrderService internally writes the Assigned OrderEvent, increments Version, commits, then publishes OrderChanged (and NewOrderOffered) after commit — the job asserts effects, it does NOT publish.

WITHIN-TICK DOUBLE-ASSIGNMENT GUARD: the per-order phase processes orders sequentially in fresh scopes, each committing before the next. When two New orders in one fleet compete for one eligible driver, order A commits Assigned first but leaves the driver Free (ApplyAssign changes no driver status). The Assumption-6 exclusion of drivers already the DriverId of an Assigned order is therefore ALSO the sole guard against assigning that same driver to order B in the SAME tick — because A's commit is visible when B's scope re-queries drivers. Implement the exclusion so exactly one of two competing orders is assigned per tick (the other stays New and is retried next tick), consistent with the spec's 'one offer at a time'.

CONCURRENCY (spec AC#4 / test 8): a manual dispatcher assign that lands first makes the job's transition a no-op — TransitionAsync returns IsSuccess == false with FailureKind StaleVersion OR IllegalTransition (the order is already Assigned when the job loads it). BOTH are caught (result.IsSuccess check, NOT an exception) and logged at Debug as a benign skip with Reason = result.FailureKind.ToString(). No exception surfaces; the order ends Assigned to the manually-chosen driver. The scan-picks-only-New filter is the first-line guard.

DI: register AutoDispatchJob as a hosted service in JobsServiceExtensions.AddJobs alongside OfferTimeoutJob (services.AddHostedService<AutoDispatchJob>();). No global kill-switch flag — per-fleet AutoDispatchEnabled is the gate (see Assumptions). Poll interval 5 s to match OfferTimeoutJob.
Quality gate: dotnet build -warnaserror and dotnet test both green. No frontend changes (the existing OrderChanged stream drives the UI).
test_cases: RunTick_NewOrderOneEligibleInRadiusDriver_AssignsToThatDriver: New order older than AutoDispatchAfterSeconds + AutoDispatchEnabled=true + one Free fresh in-radius driver → order becomes Assigned to that driver; DriverId set; exactly one Assigned OrderEvent written; (optionally assert OrderChanged via the recording publisher). Spec test 1.
RunTick_TwoEligibleDrivers_OffersNearest: two Free fresh in-radius drivers at different distances → the closer one is assigned. Spec test 2.
RunTick_DriverOutsideRadius_OrderStaysNew: only driver is beyond MaxOfferRadiusKm → order stays New, no Assigned event. Spec test 3.

RunTick_TimedOutDriverExcluded_OffersNextNearest: seed the order with a Timeout OrderEvent (payload {timedOutDriverId}) for the nearest driver (simulating the OfferTimeoutJob revert), plus a second farther eligible driver → the tick assigns the SECOND driver, not the timed-out one; a further tick with all candidates exhausted leaves the order New. Spec test 4.
RunTick_AutoDispatchDisabled_OrderUntouched: AutoDispatchEnabled=false → order stays New. RunTick_NoSettingsRow_OrderUntouched: no FleetSettings row → order stays New. Spec test 5.

RunTick_NotYetElapsed_OrderUntouched: order whose CreatedAt is LESS than AutoDispatchAfterSeconds before FixedNow → stays New. Keep FakeTime PINNED at FixedNow and set the order's CreatedAt relative to it (mirror BackgroundJobTests' assignedAt = FixedNow.AddSeconds(-46) style) — do NOT call FakeTime.Advance (advancing FakeTime is irreversible and contaminates the shared Testcontainers DB per CLAUDE.md). Spec test 5.

RunTick_TwoNewOrdersOneEligibleDriver_AssignsExactlyOne: two New eligible orders in one fleet, one Free fresh in-radius driver → exactly ONE order becomes Assigned to that driver in a single tick; the other stays New (retried next tick). This test pins the within-tick double-assignment guard (Assumption 6).
RunTick_FutureScheduledOrder_NotDispatched: New order with ScheduledAt in the future but CreatedAt older than AutoDispatchAfterSeconds → stays New (the ScheduledAt guard).
RunTick_OfflineAndStaleDriversExcluded: an Offline driver and a Free-but-stale-position driver in radius → order stays New (eligibility). Spec test 6.

RunTick_TenantIsolation_FleetBOrderUnaffected: a New eligible order in fleet B (auto-dispatch on) and a New eligible order in fleet A → dispatching runs per-fleet in the correct tenant context; the assign for fleet A does not touch fleet B's order and vice versa; each order is assigned only to a driver of its own fleet. Spec test 7 / AC#5.

RunTick_ManualAssignWinsRace_JobIsNoOp: pre-assign the order manually (order already Assigned) before the tick → TransitionAsync returns IsSuccess=false (StaleVersion or IllegalTransition), NO exception surfaces, order remains Assigned to the manually-chosen driver, no duplicate Assigned event from the job. Spec test 8 / AC#4.
work_items.notes: Mirror OfferTimeoutJob line-for-line: same ExecuteAsync shell, same scan-scope/IgnoreQueryFilters, same per-order fresh-scope + concrete CurrentTenant.FleetId, same (int?)-cast projection guard. Reuse BackgroundJobTests seed helpers (SeedFleetAndDriver, OpenNullTenantScope, FakeTime pinned to 2026-09-10 12:00 UTC) as the template for AutoDispatchJobTests. Key deltas from OfferTimeoutJob: (1) gating asymmetry — missing settings row SKIPS instead of defaulting; (2) exclusion set from Declined/Timeout payloads parsed in memory; (3) driver selection delegated to the WI-1 pure selector; (4) offer transition is Assign (needs AssignPayload with vehicle id), not Timeout. Nearest-first sequencing emerges from the OfferTimeoutJob revert loop with NO new timeout/retry state in this job — each tick is independent. Do the driver + order_events reads inside the per-order tenant scope so query filters enforce fleet isolation for free (makes the tenant-isolation test pass cleanly). Assert primary effects on DB state (Status/DriverId/Assigned event); publisher assertions are secondary.
